Relief shown by contours, hachures and spot heights. Japanese title and annotations in red and blue pencil, map drawn in black pen-and-ink. English title and annotations in red pencil and black pen-and-ink. Map shows the name of each regiment, its location and area of responsibility, along with its boundaries, and depicts road conditions and positions. Map was probably drawn by the Japanese Navy and later added translation and annotations by the U.S. Army. The Japanese Navy stationed its first garrison on Pohnpei Island in 1940, followed by a full-fledged guard in 1942, after the outbreak of the Pacific War. The U.S. military attacked Pohnpei Island on February 15, 1944, and continued through May. Seal of possession of the Japanese Navy or Army General Staff on map. Torn at fold lines. Available also through the Library of Congress Web site as a raster image. In Japanese and English. vcFY24
